geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the wing split with a courtyard operator so the mass gains a readable public void and active ground response.
Set a usable court depth that is proportionate to the compact neighborhood brief.
Align the court opening with the program access side to strengthen the public threshold.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the split-wing move into a true public court so the ground threshold becomes legible and program-fit improves.
Size the court as usable public open space rather than decorative subtraction.
Open the public void toward the verified access side to create an active frontage response.
Preserve the dominant terraced gesture while aligning the section logic to the long frontage condition.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact stepped object with a bend, and it is coherent in plan and elevation, but the actual visible massing still leans toward a generic terraced bar rather than a clearly public neighborhood building. The parcel response is only partial: the dominant gesture sits inside the boundary, yet the open-space figure is weak and the road-front edge does not resolve into a legible court, notch, or entry seam on the verified access side. The silhouette is coherent enough to avoid failure on fragmentation, but the section logic is not yet persuasive for neighborhood living because the stepped upper mass dominates more than the ground threshold. Compared with the references, it has some resonance with terraced courtyard and bridge-like campus principles, but it lacks the strong void/public ground relationship and the spatial clarity of a true active frontage. Thus program fit fails the hard pass even though the form is salvageable.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More sculptural and pavilion-like than the candidate; do not copy the curved parapet language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise terracing around a large central void can create a clear public threshold and keep one dominant mass readable.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more complex in site scale; tower elements are not transferable to this compact brief.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like courtyard organization and stepped low-rise blocks can preserve hierarchy while producing usable open space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More stretched and glazed than the candidate; avoid turning the mass into a generic bar.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: An elongated mass with a central void and slight roof articulation can support neighborhood mixed use.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More distributed and multi-winged than the candidate; do not over-fragment the mass.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced wings around a core can preserve a dominant gesture while opening public space and preserving hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Flat-roofed rectilinear campus language is not the same as this candidate's stepped compact object.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a large central void and elevated links can maintain a strong ground threshold.

warnings: Parcel containment appears acceptable in the views shown, so the failure is not from boundary violation.
The access edge response is semantically weak: no clear public void or undercut is legible along the verified road frontage.
The form is coherent across views, but the open-space organization is insufficient for the neighborhood_living brief.
The current BOOK split language adds complexity without enough public-section consequence.
